summary: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) (prospective — use of registry info in hiring); ICRAA §§1786.16, 1786.40 (prospective); FCRA §1681b(b)(3) pre-adverse, §1681d investigative reports, §1681m(a) final adverse-action notice (prospective); UCL §17200 (prospective)

counts.title: [PROSPECTIVE] Penal Code §290.46(j)(2)(E) — if Uber or TaskUs obtains or uses California sex offender registry information in the hiring decision
[PROSPECTIVE] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§1786.16 and 1786.40 — authorization/disclosure and adverse-action compliance on a consumer or investigative consumer report
[PROSPECTIVE] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. §1681b(b)(3) (pre-adverse), §1681d (investigative reports), and §1681m(a) (final adverse-action notice) if a consumer report drives the decision
[PROSPECTIVE] UCL, Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 — unlawful prong borrowing any of the above violations
